security_spec.violation_condition: XiangShan RTL implements the old (pre-fix) xiselect range check where xireg4-xireg6 raise illegal instruction only when xiselect is in 0x1000-0x1100 (inclusive) instead of the corrected 0x1000-0x10FF, AND/OR the iprio/sourcecfg indirect access array is sized for 256 entries (index 0-255) but the decode logic treats xiselect=0x1100 as a valid index, causing an off-by-one out-of-bounds access to register array index 256 for both read (xireg/xireg2/xireg3) and write paths
security_spec.summary: Spec fixes xiselect upper bound from 0x1100 to 0x10FF (off-by-one: 0x1100 was the 257th index for 256-entry arrays). If RTL hardcodes the old 0x1100 bound in range-check comparators or uses it as the last valid table index, xireg/xireg2/xireg3 access at xiselect=0x1100 reads/writes array index 256 beyond the allocated 256-entry register file, leaking adjacent hardware register state or corrupting unrelated CSR storage

findings.finding: MISelectField WARL maxValue=0xFF (line 226) prevents writing 0x1000-0x1100. The isIllegal signal at line 24 uses >= 0x100.U as out-of-range check. Since WARL write enforcement (CSRFields.scala:505) rejects values > 0xFF, xiselect=0x1000 cannot be stored in miselect. The violation condition (off-by-one range 0x1000-0x1100 vs 0x1000-0x10FF) cannot arise because no Smidctrl implementation exists in the RTL.
findings.snippet:
isIllegal :=
  value < 0x30.U ||
  value >= 0x30.U && value < 0x40.U && value(0) === 1.U ||
  value >= 0x40.U && value < 0x70.U ||
  value >= 0x100.U

spec_citations.excerpt: The registers xireg4 through xireg6 are reserved and raise an illegal instruction exception when xiselect is in the range 0x1000-0x10FF.

findings.finding: SISelectField WARL maxValue=0xFFF (line 234) accepts 0x1000-0x10FF at write time (passes legalRange [0, 0xFFF] check), but the isIllegal signal at line 51 uses >= 0x100.U, which flags 0x1000 as illegal. However, the isIllegal signal is currently declared (HasISelectBundle trait) but NOT consumed/wired to the permit module (CSRPermitModule.scala uses Iselect classification instead). The defense-in-depth works: even if isIllegal is unused, Iselect.isInOthers correctly classifies 0x1000-0x10FF as 'other' and traps on ireg access via IndirectCSRPermitModule.

findings.finding: VSISelectField WARL maxValue=0xFFF (line 217) and isIllegal using >= 0x100.U check (line 76). Same defense-in-depth as siselect: Iselect.isInOthers classification in permit module provides the runtime trap on any out-of-range iselect. No Smidctrl implementation exists, so the violation condition cannot manifest.

MISelectField WARL maxValue=0xFF. Values 0x1000-0x1100 fail the isLegal check (CSRFields.scala:505: enumeration.asUInt >= 0.U && enumeration.asUInt <= maxValue.U), so the register retains the previous legal value. Correct enforcement prevents any xiselect-like values from being written to miselect.
findings.snippet:
object MISelectField extends ISelectField(
  maxValue = 0xFF,
  reserved = Seq(
    Range.inclusive(0x00, 0x2F),
    Range.inclusive(0x40, 0x6F),
  ),
)

findings.finding: WARL legalRange for SISelectField/VSISelectField is [0, 0xFFF], but the actual usable subrange is only 0x30-0x3F and 0x70-0xFF. Values 0x100-0xFFF pass WARL write check (isLegal=true) but trap on subsequent ireg access. The reserved Seq (e.g., Range.inclusive(0x100, 0xFFF)) is DOCUMENTATION-ONLY (only used in warlConstraintDescription text), NOT enforced in isLegal hardware check (CSRFields.scala:504-505). This creates a two-layer enforcement gap: if the IndirectCSRPermitModule were modified without updating WARL, invalid iselect values would be stored. A spec-faithful Smidctrl addition would need to enforce subrange whitelisting in isLegal, not just [0, maxValue].
findings.snippet:
object SISelectField extends ISelectField(
  maxValue = 0xFFF,
  reserved = Seq(
    Range.inclusive(0x000, 0x02F),
    Range.inclusive(0x040, 0x06F),
    Range.inclusive(0x100, 0xFFF),
  ),
)

spec_citations.excerpt: Attempts to access mireg* while miselect holds a number in an allocated and implemented range results in a specific behavior that, for each combination of miselect and mireg_i, is defined by the extension to which the miselect value is allocated.

findings.finding: Iselect.isInOthers correctly classifies any iselect outside [0x30, 0x3F] U+ [0x70, 0xFF] as 'others'. Since 0x1000-0x10FF falls outside these ranges, it is correctly trapped by IndirectCSRPermitModule. If Smidctrl is implemented, isInOthers must be updated to exclude 0x1000-0x10FF. An off-by-one using >= 0x1100 instead of >= 0x10FF (if separating ranges) would fail to classify xiselect=0x1100 as 'others', allowing it to bypass trapping.

spec_citations.excerpt: The registers xireg4 through xireg6 are reserved and raise an illegal instruction exception when xiselect is in the range 0x1000-0x10FF.

findings.finding: Permit module correctly traps ireg access when iselect is in 'others' range. rwMireg_EX_II (line 531-534) raises EX_II when Iselect.isInOthers(miselect) && addr === CSRs.mireg.U. rwSireg_EX_II (line 538-553) has parallel logic for sireg. All mireg2-6, sireg2-6, vsireg2-6 accesses always trap via rwMireg2_6_EX_II / rwSireg2_6_EX_II / rwVSireg2_6_EX_II irrespective of iselect value. This is the primary runtime defense — if Smidctrl were added, these signals must be updated to NOT trap when xiselect is 0x1000-0x10FF.

spec_citations.excerpt: The behavior upon accessing mireg* from M-mode, while miselect holds a value that is not implemented, is UNSPECIFIED. [NOTE] It is expected that implementations will typically raise an illegal-instruction exception for such accesses.

findings.finding: All xireg[4:6] equivalents (mireg4-6, sireg4-6, vsireg4-6) are hardwired to 0.U via ZeroFieldBundle. These registers always trap via Ireg.isInMireg2_6/isInSireg2_6/isInVSireg2_6 in the permit module regardless of iselect value. If Smidctrl were implemented, these modules would need to become functional: xireg4=xaclicsourcecfg, xireg5=high half for RV64, xireg6=xacliciprio. The array sizing and index mapping (xiselect 0x1000-0x10FF → indices 0-255) must use the corrected upper bound; using 0x1100 as inclusive upper bound would create an off-by-one OOB access to index 256.

spec_citations.excerpt: The registers xireg4 through xireg6 are reserved and raise an illegal instruction exception when xiselect is in the range 0x1000-0x10FF.

findings.finding: Mux1H selects ireg read data from miregiprios/siregiprios arrays (addresses 0x30-0x3F only). For any iselect value not matching a prio address, all select inputs are false, so Chisel Mux1H defaults to 0.U. This means if a Smidctrl xiselect=0x1100 (off-by-one) slipped past all defenses, the read path would silently return zero from ireg rather than producing garbage or leaking state. However, the write path (NewCSR.scala:533-550) uses the same address-matching pattern, so an OOB xiselect would match no target and the write would be silently dropped.

VS-mode iselect (vsiselect) has no write-enable for xaclicsourcecfg/xacliciprio since those registers don't exist yet. The vsireg read path (line 81: regOut := iregRead.sireg) mirrors sireg data. When Smidctrl is implemented, vsiselect-aware routing for xireg[4:6] must be added for the H-extension virtual supervisor domain.

Indirect write routing uses address-matching: miregiprios.foreach { mod => mod.w.wen := mireg.w.wen && (miselect.regOut.ALL.asUInt === mod.addr.U) }. When Smidctrl adds xaclicsourcecfg/xacliciprio arrays with 256 entries (xiselect 0x1000-0x10FF → index 0-255), the write routing must map xiselect to array index via subtraction (xiselect - 0x1000). If the range check permits xiselect=0x1100, the index computation 0x1100 - 0x1000 = 256 would access past the end of a 256-entry Vec, causing write corruption to adjacent memory/logic.
findings.snippet:
miregiprios.foreach { mod =>
  mod.w.wen := mireg.w.wen && (miselect.regOut.ALL.asUInt === mod.addr.U)
  mod.w.wdata := wdata
}
